  • Native memory and spill explains the native buffers and the spill files.

items.title: Write files
items.text:
You have data in Java and want to store it as a Parquet or GeoParquet file, ready for other tools to read and filter. This guide writes a file from rows built in Java, with flat and nested columns, then a GeoParquet file with a geometry column.

It needs parquetry-core. Getting started adds the dependency and lists the JVM flags.

items.title: Write a file
items.text:
The program writes three cities to cities.parquet:

import io.tileverse.parquetry.data.ParquetFileWriter;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.data.ParquetRecordBatchBuilder;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.data.WriteOptions;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.format.LogicalType;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.io.ByteSink;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.ColumnPath;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.ParquetSchema;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.PrimitiveKind;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.Repetition;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.SchemaNode;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.OptionalInt;

public class WriteCities {

    private static final ColumnPath ID = ColumnPath.of("id");
    private static final ColumnPath NAME = ColumnPath.of("name");

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Path path = Path.of("cities.parquet");
        ParquetSchema schema = citySchema();

        try (ByteSink sink = ByteSink.ofFile(path);
                ParquetFileWriter writer = ParquetFileWriter.create(sink, schema, WriteOptions.defaults());
                ParquetRecordBatchBuilder rows = writer.appender()) {
            rows.setLong(ID, 1).setString(NAME, "Rosario").endRow();
            rows.setLong(ID, 2).setString(NAME, "Montevideo").endRow();
            rows.setLong(ID, 3).endRow();
        }
    }

    private static ParquetSchema citySchema() {
        SchemaNode.Primitive id = new SchemaNode.Primitive(
                "id", Repetition.REQUIRED, PrimitiveKind.INT64, OptionalInt.empty(), Optional.empty(), -1);
        SchemaNode.Primitive name = new SchemaNode.Primitive(
                "name",
                Repetition.OPTIONAL,
                PrimitiveKind.BYTE_ARRAY,
                OptionalInt.empty(),
                Optional.of(new LogicalType.StringType()),
                -1);
        SchemaNode.Group root =
                new SchemaNode.Group("schema", Repetition.REQUIRED, List.of(id, name), Optional.empty(), -1);
        return new ParquetSchema(root);
    }
}

It prints nothing, and leaves cities.parquet with three rows. The third city has no name: the name column is optional, and a column left unset in a row is written as null.

items.title: Describe the schema
items.text:
A schema is a tree of SchemaNode records. The root is a SchemaNode.Group, and the columns are nodes under it:

  • SchemaNode.Primitive is a column of values. Its arguments are the name, the repetition, the physical type, the byte length of a FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY column, the logical type, and the field id.
  • SchemaNode.Group holds other nodes: a struct, a list or a map. Its arguments are the name, the repetition, the children, the logical type, and the field id.

The repetition is REQUIRED, OPTIONAL or REPEATED. The logical type refines the physical type: LogicalType.StringType marks a BYTE_ARRAY column as holding UTF-8 strings. A field id of -1 means no field id.

items.title: Add rows
items.text:
writer.appender() returns a row builder bound to the writer:

  • setLong, setString, setDouble and the other setters stage the value of a column. They take a ColumnPath, or the position of the column among the leaf columns of the schema.
  • endRow() closes the row. An unset optional column is null. An unset required column fails the row with a ParquetWriteException.
  • The builder sends a batch to the writer every 8,192 rows, and when its staged values reach 16 MiB. Closing the builder, or the writer, sends the last rows.

The writer starts a new row group, the next block of rows of the file, when the current one reaches its target size. flushRowGroup() closes the current row group earlier.

items.title: Write nested columns
items.text:
The writer writes structs, lists and maps, and containers nested in each other. A struct is a group with fields. A list is a group with the LIST logical type, holding a repeated group named list, which holds the element node:

SchemaNode.Group address =
        new SchemaNode.Group("address", Repetition.OPTIONAL, List.of(city), Optional.empty(), -1);
SchemaNode.Group list =
        new SchemaNode.Group("list", Repetition.REPEATED, List.of(element), Optional.empty(), -1);
SchemaNode.Group tags = new SchemaNode.Group(
        "tags", Repetition.OPTIONAL, List.of(list), Optional.of(new LogicalType.ListType()), -1);

Here city and element are optional string columns, declared like name above. The row builder opens a scope for a nested value:

rows.setLong(ID, 1);
rows.beginStruct("address").setString(ColumnPath.of("address", "city"), "Rosario").endStruct();
rows.beginList("tags").addString("port").addString("river").endList();
rows.endRow();
  • A struct opens with beginStruct and closes with endStruct. Its fields are named by their full path.
  • A list opens with beginList and closes with endList. addString, addInt and the other add methods append a value element. A list of structs adds an element between addElement() and endElement(), and names the element fields by their path under the list, such as ColumnPath.of("element", "city").
  • A map opens with beginMap and closes with endMap. An entry sits between putEntry() and endEntry(), and its fields are ColumnPath.of("key_value", "key") and ColumnPath.of("key_value", "value").
  • A list or map with nothing added is empty. setNull(path) on the path of a struct, list or map makes it null.

The writer writes lists in the standard three-level form of the Parquet format. A list declared in an older form, such as a bare repeated column, is written in the standard form. Per-column options then name its leaf by its standard path, tags.list.element.

items.title: Write batches
items.text: writer.writeBatch(batch) appends a ParquetRecordBatch in one call. The batch columns must match the schema of the writer. A batch comes from a read, such as the batches of Read columnar batches, or from ParquetRecordBatchBuilder.forSchema(schema), which builds rows as the appender does and returns them through build().

items.title: Write a GeoParquet file
items.text:
A column becomes a geometry column when the write options give it a coordinate reference system. Its values are WKB bytes. The program writes the location of a city:

import io.tileverse.parquetry.data.ParquetFileWriter;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.data.ParquetRecordBatchBuilder;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.data.WriteOptions;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.io.ByteSink;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.ColumnPath;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.ParquetSchema;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.PrimitiveKind;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.Repetition;
import io.tileverse.parquetry.schema.SchemaNode;
import java.lang.foreign.MemorySegment;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.OptionalInt;
import org.locationtech.jts.geom.Coordinate;
import org.locationtech.jts.geom.GeometryFactory;
import org.locationtech.jts.geom.Point;
import org.locationtech.jts.io.WKBWriter;

public class WritePlaces {

    private static final ColumnPath ID = ColumnPath.of("id");
    private static final ColumnPath GEOMETRY = ColumnPath.of("geometry");

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Path path = Path.of("places.parquet");
        ParquetSchema schema = placeSchema();
        WriteOptions options = WriteOptions.builder().crsEpsg("geometry", 4326).build();
        GeometryFactory geometries = new GeometryFactory();
        WKBWriter wkb = new WKBWriter();

        try (ByteSink sink = ByteSink.ofFile(path);
                ParquetFileWriter writer = ParquetFileWriter.create(sink, schema, options);
                ParquetRecordBatchBuilder rows = writer.appender()) {
            Point rosario = geometries.createPoint(new Coordinate(-60.65, -32.95));
            MemorySegment rosarioWkb = MemorySegment.ofArray(wkb.write(rosario));
            rows.setLong(ID, 1).setBinary(GEOMETRY, rosarioWkb).endRow();
        }
    }

    private static ParquetSchema placeSchema() {
        SchemaNode.Primitive id = new SchemaNode.Primitive(
                "id", Repetition.REQUIRED, PrimitiveKind.INT64, OptionalInt.empty(), Optional.empty(), -1);
        SchemaNode.Primitive geometry = new SchemaNode.Primitive(
                "geometry", Repetition.OPTIONAL, PrimitiveKind.BYTE_ARRAY, OptionalInt.empty(), Optional.empty(), -1);
        SchemaNode.Group root =
                new SchemaNode.Group("schema", Repetition.REQUIRED, List.of(id, geometry), Optional.empty(), -1);
        return new ParquetSchema(root);
    }
}

The CRS options declare the geometry columns:

  • crsEpsg(column, code) takes an EPSG code from the bundle shipped with Parquetry, and fails for a code missing from it.
  • crs(column, projjson) takes a PROJJSON document, as a string or as a parsed CoordinateReferenceSystem.
  • crsUnknown(column) declares the CRS unknown, written as "crs": null in the geo document.

With the default options, the file has three spatial additions:

  • GeoParquet 1.1 and 2.0 metadata. The metadata mode DUAL_V1_1_AND_V2_0 writes the native Parquet GEOMETRY logical type on the column, geometry statistics per row group, and a geo document of version 1.1.0. geoParquetMetadata(GeoParquetMetadataMode.V2_0_ONLY) writes the logical type, the geometry statistics and a geo document of version 2.0.0. V1_1_ONLY writes the geo document of version 1.1.0 alone. A file in Parquet version 1.1 is always written in V1_1_ONLY.
  • A bbox covering. The writer adds a bbox struct column with the xmin, ymin, xmax and ymax of each geometry, and declares it in the geo document. A read uses these columns to skip row groups and pages, as described in Filter by location. The covering is written for the primary geometry column, the first geometry column of the schema. Its values are FLOAT for a column in OGC:CRS84 or EPSG:4326, and DOUBLE otherwise. Its pages hold at most 1,024 values, and coveringPageValueLimit(n) changes that limit.
  • Plain geometry pages. A geometry column is written without dictionary encoding, because geometries rarely repeat. Dictionary encoding stores the distinct values of a column once.

bboxCovering(CoveringMode.NONE) writes no covering, and CoveringMode.FLOAT or CoveringMode.DOUBLE forces the type of its values. The covering is written in any metadata mode, V2_0_ONLY included. A schema may already have a top-level bbox struct, as written by some GeoParquet 1.0 writers. The writer then declares that struct as the covering when it follows the GeoParquet rules for a covering column, and adds no other. existingBboxCovering(...) names the covering columns of a schema explicitly.

items.title: Choose the order of float statistics
items.text:
The min/max statistics of FLOAT, DOUBLE and FLOAT16 columns follow the type-defined order by default. The IEEE 754 total order is the order recommended by the Parquet format, and some readers in use today cannot open a file written in it. Float statistics compares the two orders and lists the readers tested.

import io.tileverse.parquetry.data.WriteOptions;

WriteOptions options = WriteOptions.builder()
        .floatColumnOrder(WriteOptions.FloatColumnOrder.IEEE_754_TOTAL_ORDER)
        .build();

The par cp command takes the same choice when it copies a file:

par cp --float-column-order ieee_754_total_order in.parquet out.parquet

The option applies to the float columns of the file, the bbox covering columns of a GeoParquet file included.

items.title: Options that matter
items.text:
WriteOptions.defaults() writes Parquet 2.0 pages, compressed with ZSTD at level 3, with a page index. The page index records the position, minimum and maximum of the pages, and lets a filtered read skip pages. WriteOptions.builder() changes one setting at a time:

Option Default What it controls parquetVersion V2_0 The page format. V1_1 writes the older data page headers, for readers that need them, and no page index. defaultCompression, compression(column, codec) Compression.zstd(3) The codec of the columns, or of one column. The writer compresses with uncompressed(), snappy(), gzip(), lz4Raw(), zstd(level) and lzo(). lzo() writes raw LZO blocks (Format support). Brotli and the deprecated LZ4 codec are read-only. rowGroupSize about 128 MB of uncompressed data RowGroupSize.bytes(n) sets another size, RowGroupSize.rows(n) a row count. pageValueLimit, pageByteLimit 8,192 values, 64 KiB The size of a data page. Smaller pages let a filter skip finer ranges of rows, and make the page index larger. encodingPolicy(column, policy) dictionary when it fits EncodingPolicy.FORCE_PLAIN writes a column without a dictionary. A column falls back to plain encoding when its dictionary passes dictionaryByteLimit, 1 MiB by default. indexedColumns(columns...), bloomFilter(column, config) none Bloom filters on the named columns, used by reads to skip row groups on eq and in predicates. keyValueMetadata(key, value) none Entries in the key/value metadata of the file. The geo key is reserved for the writer. tempDir java.io.tmpdir The directory of the temporary files of the writer.

Per-column options name a column by its dotted path, such as address.city. An option naming no column of the schema is ignored.

Lay out files for selective queries explains how row group and page sizes, the page index and the order of the rows shape the bytes fetched by a filtered read.

items.title: Finish the file
items.text:
• Close the writer, then the sink. Closing the writer writes the last row group and the footer. The writer never closes the sink: closing the sink after the writer commits the file. The samples write a local file: they declare the sink first in the try block, and Java closes the writer, then the sink.
  • On failure. A writer that fails writes no footer, and the output is not a valid Parquet file. For a local file, as in the samples, the try block still closes the sink: delete the file. A sink that commits on close behaves differently. ByteSink.ofOutputStream closes its stream, and closing an object-storage upload stream publishes the object. After a failure, do not close such a sink: abort the upload through the API of its storage instead. Keep that sink out of the try resources, and close it only after the writer closed without error. Cloud storage shows such an upload.
  • Temporary files. The writer encodes the columns of the current row group into temporary files under tempDir, and appends the row group to the sink when it is complete. Tune memory chooses their directory. The sink is written front to back only: ByteSink.ofOutputStream turns any OutputStream into a sink.
  • Threads. A writer is not thread-safe. Write to it from one thread. The writer encodes the columns of a row group in parallel, on a shared thread pool. The output bytes do not depend on that parallelism.

items.title: Format support
items.text:
This page lists the Parquet and GeoParquet features read and written by Parquetry. Use it to check whether Parquetry opens your files, and whether its output has the features needed by your readers.

Parquetry reads files of Parquet format versions 1.x and 2.x. It writes Parquet 2.0 files by default, and Parquet 1.1 files on request (Write files). Not supported lists the features known to be missing.

items.title: Pages
items.text:
A row group is a block of rows of the file. A column chunk holds the values of one column in a row group, and is cut into pages. A dictionary page holds the distinct values of the chunk, and data pages hold the values or their positions in the dictionary.

Feature Read Write Data pages, version 1 (DATA_PAGE) yes yes, in Parquet 1.1 files Data pages, version 2 (DATA_PAGE_V2) yes yes, in Parquet 2.0 files Dictionary pages yes yes

items.title: Physical types
items.text:
Type Read Write BOOLEAN, INT32, INT64, FLOAT, DOUBLE yes yes BYTE_ARRAY, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY yes yes

Parquetry also reads INT96, the legacy timestamp type of files written by Spark and Impala.

items.title: Logical types
items.text:
A logical type tells how to interpret the values of a physical type, such as a STRING stored as BYTE_ARRAY.

Logical type Read STRING, ENUM, JSON, BSON, UUID yes INT, signed and unsigned, of 8 to 64 bits yes DECIMAL yes DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP in milliseconds, microseconds and nanoseconds yes FLOAT16 yes VARIANT, shredded and unshredded yes GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY yes, see GeoParquet LIST, MAP yes, see Nested types The converted types of older writers, such as UTF8 and TIMESTAMP_MILLIS yes

The writer writes the logical types declared in the schema of the file. It also writes the matching converted type, when one exists, for readers older than logical types. A VARIANT column is written shredded or unshredded, as declared in the schema.

items.title: Encodings
items.text:
An encoding is the layout of the values in a page.

Encoding Read Write PLAIN yes yes Dictionary: RLE_DICTIONARY, and PLAIN_DICTIONARY of older writers yes yes: RLE_DICTIONARY in Parquet 2.0 files, PLAIN_DICTIONARY in Parquet 1.1 files RLE, for repetition and definition levels yes yes RLE, for BOOLEAN values yes no DELTA_BINARY_PACKED, for INT32 and INT64 yes no DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY and DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY, for BYTE_ARRAY yes no BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT, for FLOAT and DOUBLE yes no ALP, for FLOAT and DOUBLE yes no

The writer encodes a column with a dictionary while the dictionary stays under its size limit, and with PLAIN beyond it.

items.title: Compression
items.text:
Codec Read Write UNCOMPRESSED, SNAPPY, GZIP, ZSTD, LZ4_RAW yes yes BROTLI yes no LZO, as raw LZO blocks yes yes LZ4, deprecated by the format, in the Hadoop framing or as raw blocks yes no

The LZO codec reads and writes raw LZO blocks, without the stream framing of Hadoop. Files from writers using the Hadoop LZO framing are not tested.

items.title: Statistics and indexes
items.text:
Feature Read Write Column chunk statistics: minimum, maximum, null count yes, to skip row groups yes Float statistics in type-defined order or in IEEE 754 total order, with NaN counts yes, to skip row groups and pages type-defined order by default, total order on request Page index: column index and offset index yes, to skip pages yes, in Parquet 2.0 files Split block bloom filters yes, to skip row groups on eq and in filters yes, on the columns named in the write options

A page index records the position, minimum and maximum of the pages of a column chunk. When a file has none, a read learns the pages of a row group from their headers, and later reads of that row group skip pages with them (Without a page index). Float statistics explains the two orders for floating-point columns.

items.title: Nested types
items.text: Feature Read Write Structs yes yes Lists and maps in the standard three-level form yes yes Lists and maps inside lists, maps and structs yes yes Lists and maps in the forms of older writers, such as two-level lists and repeated fields outside a list yes written in the standard form

items.title: GeoParquet
items.text:
GeoParquet stores geometries in Parquet columns, and describes them in a geo document in the key/value metadata of the file. Version 2.0 also uses the GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY logical types of Parquet.

Feature Read Write geo document, version 1.0.0 yes no, Parquetry writes 1.1.0 geo document, version 1.1.0 yes yes, by default geo document, version 2.0.0 yes on request Geometries encoded as WKB yes yes GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY logical types yes GEOMETRY, by default Geometry statistics per row group, the bounding box of the geometries yes, to skip row groups yes, with the GEOMETRY logical type bbox covering columns, the bounding box of each geometry in four columns yes, to skip row groups and pages yes, by default A bbox struct without a covering declaration, as written by some GeoParquet 1.0 writers yes, used as a covering declared as the covering Coordinate reference systems as PROJJSON yes yes

Write files shows the metadata modes and the covering options. Read GeoParquet reads the geometries and the geo document.

items.title: Not supported
items.text:
• Modular encryption. Parquetry does not decrypt files, and writes no encrypted files.
  • Page checksums. A read does not verify the CRC checksum of a page, and the writer writes none.
  • Some encodings. BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT on INT32, INT64 and FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY columns, and DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY on FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY columns. A read of a page in one of these encodings fails with an error. The deprecated BIT_PACKED encoding of repetition and definition levels is not supported either.
  • Native GeoParquet 1.1 encodings. GeoParquet 1.1 allows geometries stored as nested structs of coordinates instead of WKB. Parquetry does not decode these columns into geometries.

items.title: Modules
items.text:
This page lists the artifacts published by Parquetry, with what each one is for and its status. Use it to choose the dependencies of your project.

The artifacts share one version number. Getting started gives the latest release and shows how to import the BOM.

items.title: Artifacts
items.text:
Declare the Parquetry modules called by your code. Maven resolves the modules below them, such as parquetry-format under parquetry-core.

Group id Artifact id Use it to Status io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-core Read and write single Parquet and GeoParquet files, filter rows, and decode geometries to JTS. stable io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-catalog Read a directory or a glob of Parquet files as one dataset. stable io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-geotools Serve GeoParquet files as GeoTools features, through a GeoTools data store. stable io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-arrow Export a read as an Arrow IPC stream or through the Arrow C Data Interface. stable io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-iceberg Read Apache Iceberg tables as datasets. experimental io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-stac Read the GeoParquet files of a STAC collection as one dataset. experimental io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-avro Read and write Avro container files, the format of Iceberg manifests and manifest lists. supporting io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-jackson Render the rows of a read as JSON. supporting io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-io Read byte ranges from files and from tileverse-storage, and pool the native buffers of reads. foundation io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-compression Compress and decompress Parquet pages and Avro blocks. foundation io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-format Decode and encode the Parquet footer and page headers, and model the schema and the GeoParquet metadata. foundation io.tileverse.parquetry.apps par Inspect, filter and copy files from the command line. experimental
  • Stable parts are ready for production use. Experimental parts work, but their API and behavior may still change. The home page explains both labels.
  • Supporting modules have no status of their own. parquetry-iceberg depends on parquetry-avro, and the par tool depends on parquetry-jackson.
  • Foundation modules sit under parquetry-core, which depends on all three. Declare parquetry-core, and Maven adds them.
  • parquetry-geotools also registers the Iceberg and STAC GeoParquet stores. These two stores read through parquetry-iceberg and parquetry-stac, and are experimental like them.
  • par is not published to Maven Central. It builds from the source repository, as The par command line tool shows.

items.title: BOMs
items.text:
Two BOMs keep versions in line. Import them in the dependencyManagement section of your POM, with <type>pom</type> and <scope>import</scope>.

Group id Artifact id Pins the versions of io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-bom The Parquetry modules listed above, except par. io.tileverse.parquetry parquetry-dependencies The third-party libraries used by Parquetry, such as tileverse-storage, JTS and Jackson.

Import parquetry-bom alone to pin the Parquetry modules. Import parquetry-dependencies as well to also align the versions of the libraries shared by your application and Parquetry.

items.title: Which module for which task
items.text:
You want to Declare Read or write one Parquet or GeoParquet file parquetry-core, plus a tileverse-storage module for object storage (Cloud storage) Read many files as one dataset parquetry-catalog Publish GeoParquet through GeoTools or GeoServer parquetry-geotools (GeoTools and GeoServer) Hand rows to an analytics engine as Arrow parquetry-arrow (Arrow interop) Print rows as JSON parquetry-jackson (JSON) Read Avro container files parquetry-avro (Avro) Read an Iceberg table or a STAC collection parquetry-iceberg or parquetry-stac (Experimental parts)

Start the JVM of your application with the flags listed in Getting started. Some modules use Java 25 preview features and fail to load without them.
